Vectorized switch (SAS select-when maps)

Source: R/vswitch.r
ks_vswitch.Rd

Looks up each element of `x` among the named values of `...` — a `switch()` that works on a whole vector at once, like SAS `select(when ...)` or a format-driven recode.

Usage

ks_vswitch(.x, ..., .na = NULL, .default = NULL)

Arguments

.x

A vector of lookup keys (character, factor, or numeric; coerced with as.character() for matching).

...

Named values of a **single common type** — the names are keys, the values are results. `vapply()` errors when the types disagree.

.na

Value returned where `x` is `NA`; defaults to an `NA` of the same type as the first value of `...`.

.default

Value returned for keys present in `x` but absent from `...`; defaults to an `NA` of the same type as the first value of `...`.

Value

A vector the same length as `.x` with the storage type of the values in `...`. The key argument is named `.x` (leading dot) so that bare case names like `x = ...` in dots cannot collide with it.

Examples

ks_vswitch(c("a", "b", "a", NA, "zz"), a = 10L, b = 20L)
#> [1] 10 20 10 NA NA
ks_vswitch(c("a", "b", NA, "zz"), a = 10L, b = 20L, .na = 0L, .default = -1L)
#> [1] 10 20  0 -1
ks_vswitch(factor(c("x", "y")), x = 1.5, y = 2.5)
#> [1] 1.5 2.5
